name: infra_jax_flax
title: JAX / Flax / optax trainer - a framework MLView deliberately does not model
origin: hardening round 1, tester domain-infra: the unsupported-framework negative
note: The point of this program is that MLView recognises NOTHING here and says so rather than guessing. It reports zero findings - correct - and emits an `unresolved_callee` diagnostic naming the four Flax layer calls it could not resolve. It does draw `train` and `eval` (from train_step / eval_step and the epoch and batch loops) and declares data, preprocess, model, objective and deliver absent, which is honest for a framework it does not carry: every op it would have needed is an optax / flax / jax call it has no table for. Every row below is a forbidden guard against a rule inventing a torch/sklearn/keras reading of a JAX symbol.

forbidden.why: there is no sklearn transformer anywhere; the only normalisation is optax's own and the chronological cut at line 102 is a plain slice
there is no torch DataLoader; batches() at line 84 permutes with a numpy Generator when shuffle=True
the validation pass calls batches(..., shuffle=False) at line 114
JAX is functional: there are no gradient buffers to zero. state.apply_gradients returns a new state rather than mutating one
state.apply_gradients(grads=grads) at line 71 is the update; jax.value_and_grad is the backward
there is no torch.no_grad in this file and no torch autograd at all
nothing accumulates a torch tensor; the metrics are jnp arrays collected per batch and stacked once
Flax has no train/eval module flag: `train=False` is passed explicitly to apply_fn at line 79, which is the JAX equivalent and is done
there is no autograd graph to disable; eval_step is a jitted pure function
optax.softmax_cross_entropy takes logits by contract and the model's last layer (line 46) is a bare nn.Dense with no activation
JAX places arrays on the default device; there is no .to()/.cuda() model/batch split to get wrong
jax.random.PRNGKey(SEED) at line 97 and numpy.random.default_rng(SEED) at line 98 seed both randomness sources this program uses
the train/validation cut at lines 102-104 is a deterministic slice, not a randomised splitter
flax.linen.Module is a dataclass-style module with no __init__ of its own to chain; MLP declares fields, not a constructor
there is no torch nn.Module in this file, so there is no parameter registry to miss
